title: The form that reloaded the page

terminal.description: The route board runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell is in your workspace if you want to look around.

tasks.title: Keep the page on submit
tasks.description:
Write `watchForm(form, { isTaken, onAdd })` in `src/form.js`. It listens for `submit` on the form `#new-route` and:

- stops the browser from leaving the page
- reads the fields with `FormData`: `name`, `grade`, `colour` and `setter`
- calls `onAdd({ name, grade, colour, setter })`, with spaces trimmed from the name and the setter

`main.js` already passes an `onAdd` that puts the route on top of the board. The check fills the form, submits it and then ticks the new route.
nextSteps: Submit the form in the Browser panel and watch the board start over.
Add a `submit` listener to `form` and stop the default action first.
Make a `FormData` from the form and read the four fields by their `name`.
Call `onAdd` with an object of the four values.
hints: Submitting a form is a navigation: the browser sends the fields to a new page. You need to cancel that.
The event passed to your listener has a method that cancels what the browser would do next.
`new FormData(form).get('grade')` reads a field by its `name` attribute, selects included. Trim the text fields before you pass them on.

tasks.title: Explain bad input
tasks.description:
Some input passes the browser's `required` check but is still wrong. Before calling `onAdd`, refuse it with a plain sentence in `

` (it starts hidden): - a name that is empty once spaces are trimmed - a name already on the board, in any letter case (`isTaken(name)` tells you) A refused route is not added and the page does not reload. After a good route is added, `#form-error` is hidden again.
nextSteps: Type only spaces as a name and submit. Notice that the browser lets it through.
Work out the message, or an empty string when the input is fine.
Show or hide `#form-error` from that and stop when there is a problem.
Try a name from the board in capitals.
hints: Your checks belong after the default action is stopped and the fields are read, but before `onAdd`.
Keep one variable for the problem. Set its text on `#form-error` and its `hidden` from whether it is empty.
Return early from the listener when there is a problem, so nothing below runs. Write the message as a short sentence, such as what is missing.

tasks.title: Ready for the next route
tasks.description:
Setters log several routes in a row. After a route is added:

- the form is cleared, so `#route-name` and `#route-setter` are empty
- the focus is back in `#route-name`

After a refused route, the fields keep what was typed so it can be fixed.
nextSteps: Add two routes in a row in the Browser panel and notice what you have to delete by hand.
Move the focus to the name field.
Check that a refused route still keeps its fields.
hints: Forms have a method that puts every field back to its starting value.
Any field can take the focus with a method call. `form.elements.name` is the name field.
Do both only on the success path, after `onAdd`, never before the early return.
